question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{8p}-2p.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{8p}-2p,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{4p}{\sqrt{8p}+2p} & = \\ -\frac{4p}{\sqrt{8p}+2p}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{8p}-2p}{\sqrt{8p}-2p} & = \\ -\frac{4p(\sqrt{8p}-2p)}{(\sqrt{8p}+2p)(\sqrt{8p}-2p)} & = \\ -\frac{4p(\sqrt{8p}-2p)}{(\sqrt{8p})^{2}-(2p)^{2}} & = \\ -\frac{4p(\sqrt{8p}-2p)}{8p-4{p}^{2}} & = \\ -\frac{\cancel{4p}(\sqrt{8p}-2p)}{\cancel{4p}(2-p)} & = \\ -\frac{\sqrt{8p}-2p}{2-p}\end{aligned}
$$
